0.title: Perspectives on AI and Analytics
0.content: If you are interested in how data science and AI actually get built in the real world — where business constraints, data quality, and operating models matter as much as modeling technique — this is the place to start. I write about the gap between the polished story of AI and the practical work of producing reliable, explainable, and operationally useful systems. Recent Essays . | Beyond the Agent Illusion: Leveraging AI Systems for Real Operational Value A comparison of two ways to build intelligent systems: the AI-first, agentic view and the data-science view. The essay argues that while there are niches such as self-driving cars and robotics where the agentic approach is essential, most enterprise operations are better served by the data-science view when decisions must be explained, trusted, and understood by business operators. | Data Scientist vs ML Engineer A practical look at the different responsibilities of data scientists and machine learning engineers, where their work overlaps, and how both roles contribute to building reliable systems that create operational value. | From Business Use Case to Technical Implementation Turning business problems into tractable analytical systems, with attention to constraints, data realities, and measurable outcomes. | From Task-Specific Data to Modeling How raw operational data becomes the modeling substrate, and why task framing matters as much as the algorithm. | Modeling and Featurization The design choices that shape model quality, especially where feature engineering determines whether the system captures signal or noise. | Why using AI to understand technical content needs care and deliberation Why generative AI can flatten nuanced technical material if it is treated as a substitute for careful reading and domain judgment. | tseda: Analyst-Guided Time-Series Decomposition — An open Python package for decomposing operational time series into interpretable components such as trend, seasonality, and noise, with explicit, repeatable, and reviewable diagnostics. | . These essays are intended to be practical, opinionated, and grounded in applied analytics rather than hype. They sit alongside the consulting and methodology work on this site, and they are meant to help teams think more clearly about where data science adds value and where it does not.

2.title: Statistical Approaches for Operational Decisions
2.content: I help CTOs and engineering leaders turn operational data into analytical systems that are statistically defensible, auditable, and maintainable. The underlying platform remains open and client-owned through KMDS and tseda, so the team keeps the engine without permanent platform lock-in. I am not selling a subscription. I am selling the judgment that created the architecture in the first place and the expertise required to keep it honest as the data-generating process changes. Book a call · Read the methodology · Read the perspectives . This is a direct advisory model for organizations that need analytical rigor, not vendor dependency. I provide the initial mathematical architecture, the drift and gap analysis, and the ongoing calibration required to keep the model aligned with reality. The solution is transparent: it is built in open-source tooling that the client can inspect, run, and adapt without dependency. See the methodology for how the work is structured, and the Perspectives on AI and Analytics for examples of how these systems are thought about in real operational settings. The Open-Platform Advisory Framework . The Core Principle . I help organizations convert operational complexity into rigorous statistical learning problems without proprietary platform lock-in. The framework is built for transparency, auditability, and long-term client ownership. Where I Engage . | Phase 1: Solution Mapping — I translate physical, industrial, or enterprise use cases into tractable statistical learning problems and build feature sets that reflect the real operating system rather than superficial proxy variables. | Phase 2: Drift & Gap Analysis — I identify when data drift, concept drift, or structural degradation are beginning to invalidate model assumptions. | Phase 3: Remediation & Calibration — I rework feature definitions, decomposition windows, and model assumptions so the analytical system remains stable and decisionally valid in production. | . The Open Assets . | KMDS: A knowledge-centric framework for transparent, reproducible machine learning workflows and operationally grounded feature definition. | tseda: A Python package for analyst-guided time-series decomposition, allowing teams to separate trend, seasonality, and noise while preserving explicit statistical traceability. | . Why This Model Is Technically Credible . | The solution is transparent — it is built in an open-source framework that the client can inspect, run, and adapt without vendor dependency. | Problem framing is the first hard problem — the work begins by mapping the business question to the right set of statistical tasks, defining the validation methodology that proves the framing is right, and establishing the monitoring approach that keeps the system honest as it operates. Foundation models can give a team a baseline, but building a solution that customers and modelers truly understand and can maintain is a different question. | Monitoring and maintenance are a core part of the solution — another critical dimension of a sustainable machine learning or statistical learning system is how we monitor performance, detect when the operating environment has changed, and know when it is time to change the model or the underlying assumptions. | The engagement is about decision quality, not labor arbitrage — I am not positioned as a generic software vendor or a body-for-hire. I work as a specialist in analytical architecture, modeling rigor, and operational stewardship. | The value is ongoing stewardship — the work is framed around mathematical design, calibration, and maintenance so the analytical system remains honest as the operating environment changes. | . Perspectives on AI and Analytics . I write practical, grounded commentary on the real work of building useful AI and analytics systems: where the business problem starts, how the data becomes a model, and what it takes to turn a promising idea into something reliable enough to operate. If you are interested in my perspectives on AI — especially how generative AI and LLM tools can complement a data scientist in real analytical work — see the Perspectives on AI and Analytics page. Consulting Offering . I work with CTOs, VP-level engineering leaders, and operating teams that already have the data but do not yet have a statistically defensible architecture for turning it into reliable decisions. My work begins with the question most technical programs skip: what is the actual decision process, and what statistical structure is required to keep that decision valid as the operating environment changes? . You bring the business context, the operational history, and the pressure to make better decisions at scale. I translate that context into feature engineering, model structure, and analytical architecture that are explainable, auditable, and sustainable. Because the foundation is open and owned by your organization, the resulting analytical logic remains inside the company rather than being trapped inside a vendor platform. The highest-value engagements are not general software delivery projects. They are focused advisory engagements around featurization, model mapping, and drift remediation. I design feature sets, interaction terms, correlation-adjusted signals, and transaction- or sensor-ready datasets that improve model quality and create a more defensible operating system for production decisions. For many organizations, the most valuable work is mathematical maintenance: determining whether the model is still measuring the same thing, whether the feature definitions still reflect the actual process, and whether recalibration is required before the system drifts into poor decisions that are difficult to trace back to their source. 7.title: Open-Platform Advisory Methodology
7.content: I help organizations build and maintain analytical systems around operational business data using a disciplined open-platform framework. The objective is not to rent a software stack; it is to design the statistical architecture, preserve the analytical knowledge that makes the system durable, and maintain model validity as the operating environment evolves. The Open-Platform Advisory Framework . | Map the operational process and decision cadence to a well-posed statistical problem. | Analyze the current datasets, quality issues, and operational constraints. | Design a maintainable analytical structure using open, auditable frameworks such as KMDS and tseda. | Build reusable feature engineering components that remain inside the client organization. | Diagnose drift, concept changes, and structural degradation before they produce bad decisions. | Preserve analytical knowledge for repeatable execution and long-term maintenance. | . Engagement Phases . | Initial Solution Mapping — Define the problem, entities, features, and model framing. | Drift & Gap Analysis — Evaluate whether the underlying assumptions still hold as the data-generating process changes. | Remediation & Calibration — Rebuild the feature definitions, decomposition windows, and model assumptions when necessary. | Mathematical Maintenance — Sustain the analytical system after initial deployment. | . Step 1: Understand the Data . Questions: . | What is the unit of analysis? | What entities exist? | What temporal structure exists? | What is the baseline data quality? | Where are the drift signals likely to appear? | . Tools: . | Time-series diagnostics | Dataset profiling | Feature lineage review | . Step 2: Understand the Business Process . Questions: . | What decisions are being made? | What relationships matter? | What patterns are stable? | What assumptions are economically valuable to preserve? | . Tools: . | KMDS component analysis | Operational process mapping | Statistical dependency review | . Step 3: Build Analytical Assets . Questions: . | What features matter? | What models are appropriate? | What operational assumptions need to be explicit? | What is the maintenance plan when drift emerges? | . Tools: . | Featurization | Modeling governance | Open-source analytical implementation | . Step 4: Preserve and Maintain the Mathematical System . Questions: . | What was learned? | What assumptions were made? | How is the solution maintained over time? | Where is the model at risk of drifting from physical reality? | . Tools: . | KMDS | tseda | Drift analysis and calibration protocols | . Typical Engagement Outcomes . | A clear analytical architecture for the business problem | Reusable and auditable feature definitions | Explicit model assumptions and operational limits | Drift diagnosis and remediation plans | Durable knowledge ownership inside the client organization | . My consulting and methodological design experience spans the US, India, and Europe. For practical examples, explore the KMDS migration repository.
